He belonged to the group of astronomers associated with the Maragheh observatory in the Ilkhanate, most notably Nasir al-Din al-Tusi. entities.summary:
Muḥyī al‐Milla wa al‐Dīn Yaḥyā Abū ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al‐Shukr al‐Maghribī al‐Andalusī, referred to in sources as Muhyi l'din, was an astronomer, astrologer and mathematician of the Islamic Golden Age. He belonged to the group of astronomers associated with the Maragheh observatory in the Ilkhanate, most notably Nasir al-Din al-Tusi. In astronomy, Muhyi l'din carried out a large‐scale project of systematic planetary observations, which led to the development of several new astronomic tools and techniques. His work had significant regional impact on Islamic astronomical knowledge during the 13th century.

Born in 1220 in Al-Andalus, Spain, Muḥyī al‐Milla wa al‐Dīn spent most of his life studying at the Maragheh observatory in present-day Iran. His extensive research and observations significantly advanced Islamic astronomy during this period.

Muḥyī l'din's contributions to astronomy had far-reaching consequences, influencing the work of later astronomers such as Al-Ulugh Beg in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. His work also contributed to the development of new astronomical instruments and techniques that were adopted by other cultures, demonstrating the significant impact of Islamic Golden Age scholars on global knowledge.

 Muḥyī l'din's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of his astronomical tools and methods on modern astronomy. His contributions to the field of astronomy are still studied and referenced today, a testament to the enduring significance of his work during the 13th century Islamic Golden Age.

In 1283, Muḥyī l'din passed away in Maragheh, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of astronomical knowledge for centuries to come.
